title: Alaska: establish the franchise exclusion before using the opportunity-filing track
description: The official chapter separates a Part 436 franchise exclusion from nonexempt business-opportunity registration, buyer rights and recurring duties.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Test the express exclusion before selecting a form
paragraphs: The complete official AS 45.66.220 text excludes “a franchise under 16 C.F.R. Part 436” from this business-opportunity chapter. Establish whether the actual arrangement fits that wording before using the registration calendar. This chapter exclusion does not remove federal franchise duties or prove that no other Alaska law applies.

AS 45.66.900 has its own business-opportunity definition, including specified location/account assistance, buyback, assured-income/refund and marketing-plan promises. Section .220 contains other exclusions. Its separate mark and financial-condition branch is not established by using the word licence or holding a foreign trademark. Record the exact branch and supporting facts.

sections.heading: For a covered nonexempt offer, start with the acknowledgement
paragraphs: AS 45.66.010 requires registration at least 30 days before the sale or offer begins. Under .020(c), registration is not complete until the seller receives the department acknowledgement. Submitting an application 30 days before the campaign is therefore not, by itself, proof that the statutory condition is met.

The registration packet includes the disclosure statement, promotional materials, required bond, consent and application. AS 45.66.080 and 9 AAC 16.020 require the purchaser disclosure at least 10 calendar days before the earlier specified signature or receipt of consideration. Keep any independently applicable federal clock separate.

sections.heading: A 2005 form date is not the whole version check
paragraphs: The currently served 9 AAC 16 expressly adopts the February 9, 2005 registration, disclosure, bond and change forms by reference. Their age alone does not establish that they are obsolete. Use the incorporated form with the applicable statutory and administrative text; do not invent an online submission route or assume that preparation equals acknowledgement.

sections.heading: Own the continuing duties on the nonexempt track
paragraphs: AS 45.66.030 requires annual renewal by the initial acknowledgement anniversary while the seller continues the stated offers or sales. Section .050 requires material-change reporting within 10 days; 9 AAC 16.060 specifies the change form and delivery methods. Its listed material events include payment, management, ownership, obligation, bond and significant litigation changes.
The required bond has a different duration: 9 AAC 16.030 requires it during offers/sales and for three years after the last sale. A campaign closing date is not a bond-release date.

sections.heading: Do not waive the covered buyer’s contract rights
paragraphs: For a nonexempt opportunity, .090 requires a written contract with specified terms. Section .130 permits written cancellation for any reason within 30 days after signing and lists additional cancellation grounds. It requires seller refunds and termination of buyer financial obligations within 15 days after notice, with supplied items made available by the buyer within five days after receiving the refund. Section .170 prohibits and voids waivers of the buyer’s chapter rights or defenses.

These are scoped business-opportunity rights. They are not a general statement that every Alaska franchise has a 30-day cancellation right, nor a complete survey of franchise renewal, transfer or termination law.

sections.heading: Fictional example: an equipment-backed service launch
paragraphs: A fictional Dutch facilities brand supplies equipment, marketing support and a promise of customer accounts. Its coordinator inventories those promises, the selling entity and Alaska connections, then records the applicable exclusion or nonexempt route. On the latter route, sales uses the received acknowledgement and purchaser delivery dates; finance owns security and the cancellation/refund workflow. This fictional example does not decide classification.

sections.heading: Keep an evidence packet, not a single exemption checkbox
bullets: Exact federal relationship mapping and AS 45.66 exclusion rationale.
Offer origin, receipt, acceptance, purchaser domicile and operation facts under .070.
Acknowledgement receipt, first covered offer, disclosure receipt and commitment dates.
Current contract promises, cancellation notice, refund and item-return responsibilities.
Annual anniversary, material-change intake and bond/last-sale record.
The official compilation label and a task to check later session laws and relevant cases.

practicalOutput: An Alaska classification record, acknowledgement-based offer calendar and nonexempt contract/change checklist.
limitations: The ordinary BASIS navigation labels its served statutory compilation Alaska Statutes 2025. The complete chapter and administrative print bodies were read in this audit; a comprehensive later-2026 session-law or case-law update review is not represented.
The stated chapter, exclusion and nonexempt procedures answer separate scoped questions. Other state franchise, dealer, professional, employment, tax and local branches remain independent.
No transaction, exclusion or commencement of offers is approved by this educational guide.

title: Louisiana: the trademark wording does not settle every opportunity trigger
description: Specified device-location, buyback and earnings promises need separate screening; bond duties have their own limited scope.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Read the whole definition
paragraphs: RS 51:1821 contains registered-mark wording within a particular sales/marketing-plan provision. It separately describes assistance with specified vending, display or amusement-device locations, along with buyback and earnings/refund representations. The registered-mark phrase should not be converted into a universal exemption from every business-opportunity trigger.

sections.heading: The bond rule has its own boundary
paragraphs: RS 51:1822 specifies distinct seller and agent bonds and requires covered bonds before business, including advertising or soliciting. Its subsection G limits those requirements to opportunities defined in 51:1821(1)(a),(b) or (c). That boundary matters: a rule for one kind of offer is not a blanket bond requirement for every licensing model.

sections.heading: Carry written promises and bond changes into operations
paragraphs: For a covered business opportunity, RS 51:1823(6) requires the written agreement to include material oral statements, representations and promises made before execution; (7) prohibits a waiver of the purchaser’s legal rights. Preserve the sales record alongside the operating agreement instead of assuming the signature erases earlier promises.

For the opportunities actually subject to the bond requirement, RS 51:1822(H) makes the bond continuous. Its surety termination route requires 60 days written notice to the specified official and principal, and preserves the stated liability. This is a bond notice, not a franchise-contract exit period. Section (E) requires new or additional bonds before continuing business.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a German equipment-service package
paragraphs: The seller licences a registered mark, supplies equipment and promises to buy back output if the operator is dissatisfied. The manager records each promise separately instead of stopping at the mark. The reviewer tests each statutory trigger and any resulting seller/agent role. Sales operations retains substantiation and puts the actual promises into the written contract where required.

sections.heading: A regulated sector can add an earlier task
paragraphs: RS 37:1465 separately requires the described franchisor dealing with a Louisiana real-estate broker to appoint a Louisiana-licensed broker representative before entering that franchise agreement. This is a specific professional-sector rule, not an assumption that every property-related service is a real-estate brokerage.

sections.heading: Prepare before promotion
bullets: Goods/services, payments and every specified device-location, income, refund or buyback promise.
Exact definition limb and bond applicability, including agent role.
Earnings support and actual seller identification in covered advertising.
Service-of-process appointment and written promises.
Professional-sector review for the actual activity.

practicalOutput: A Louisiana trigger-by-trigger sales-model screen with independent bond and sector tasks.
limitations: This page addresses its named decision, not a complete state legal survey. Unknown dimensions remain unresolved in the coverage register.
Model classification, state connections, sector-dealer laws, local requirements and the actual transaction need independent review. No sale, exemption, worker status or contract term is approved.

title: Maine: the first sales meeting can matter before the contract date
description: Covered business opportunities have separate promotion, disclosure, security and avoidance tasks; the mark exception is limited.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Classify the actual promise
paragraphs: Maine’s current Title 32 Chapter 69-B describes business-opportunity triggers, including particular location, buyback, earnings/refund and marketing assistance. The federally registered-mark wording qualifies the marketing-program limb. It does not, by itself, erase every other trigger. The official PDF states currency through October 1, 2026 and that it is not the certified annotated text.

sections.heading: Do not calendar only payment
paragraphs: For a covered opportunity, 4696 requires registration before selling, offering, advertising or promotion. Section 4692 places disclosure at the earliest specified 72-hour pre-agreement/pre-payment event or the first face-to-face sales meeting. The meeting is therefore a real dependency to check rather than an assumed unrestricted discovery event.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Finnish specialist-service system
paragraphs: The brand plans an in-person pitch and equipment package. Its coordinator collects the proposed advertisement, meeting purpose, assistance promises, payments and agreement. The responsible reviewer establishes coverage and each early event before the team commits funds or tells a prospect that the registered mark settles state treatment.

sections.heading: Include the post-signature work
paragraphs: For a covered opportunity, 4698 provides a three-full-business-day avoidance process with return obligations. The chapter also addresses financial security, annual registration and exceptions. Those events are distinct from federal franchise disclosure and from operational permits.

sections.heading: Separate material changes from the annual expiry
paragraphs: Section 4696 requires updating the disclosure statement as material information changes. Section 4697 makes registration effective for one year from effectiveness, with annual renewal using a current disclosure statement, the required fee and qualifying security evidence. Failure to renew expires registration. The management calendar should therefore contain both event intake and an expiry record.

sections.heading: Build a dependency record
bullets: Actual statutory trigger and any exclusion, with evidence.
Promotion, first face-to-face meeting, signature and payment dates.
Disclosure version, registration and any applicable financial security.
Avoidance notice/return procedure and responsible person.
Current forms, certified text and case-specific interpretation for review.

practicalOutput: A Maine promotion-to-contract timeline with the first meeting and avoidance process visible.
limitations: This page addresses its named decision, not a complete state legal survey. Unknown dimensions remain unresolved in the coverage register.

title: Nevada: do not copy farm-equipment dealer rules into every franchise
description: A product-and-parts arrangement may create a relationship workstream beyond the brand agreement.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the defined inventory and agreement
paragraphs: Nevada NRS 597.112–597.118 covers defined farm-equipment dealer relationships. It identifies retail inventory rights, a distribution-system role and substantial dependence on a supplier. Its inventory definition is farm equipment and attachments or repair parts; it is not a general definition covering every maintenance service or software license.

sections.heading: The exit requires more than a contract date
paragraphs: Section 597.1143 addresses good cause and generally requires 180 days written reasons before termination/nonrenewal, with 60 days to correct specified deficiencies. Several listed grounds are treated differently, and market-share failures have an assistance condition. A company should not assume that a broadly drafted contractual termination right answers these statutory questions.

sections.heading: A substantial term change has its own coverage question
paragraphs: NRS 597.1143(1) requires good cause not only for termination or nonrenewal, but also for a substantial change to a covered dealer agreement. Section 597.115(4) addresses those actions because of natural disaster, labor dispute or similar circumstances beyond the dealer’s control. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver or modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.

The 180-day notice and 60-day correction provisions in .1143(2)–(3) concern termination and nonrenewal. Do not invent a universal 180-day notice for every amendment. Preserve the actual before-and-after terms and the reason for the proposed action.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a European equipment business
paragraphs: A manufacturer plans a Nevada operator that sells agricultural machines, holds parts and supplies branded servicing. Finance and operations should separately model inventory exposure, warranty responsibilities and continuing parts access. That work differs from licensing a pure consulting service.

sections.heading: Keep return values conditional
paragraphs: The chapter has repurchase rules and exclusions involving inventory condition, age and other facts, as well as specified supplier-required systems and tools. The company should retain evidence instead of assuming every inventory or technology cost will be reimbursed. Statutory nonwaiver provisions also deserve review.

sections.heading: Prepare the relationship file
bullets: List actual equipment, parts, suppliers and dealer rights.
Record inventory purchase dates, condition, catalogue status and invoices.
Document required systems, tools, warranty work and payment evidence.
Preserve performance notices, support offered and any proposed cure.
Assign sector-specific review; leave general franchise sales/filing coverage open until researched.

practicalOutput: A farm-equipment dealer-scope decision and inventory/exit evidence checklist.
limitations: This page researches the named issue; it is not a complete state franchise or operating-law survey.
Federal disclosure and any independent state sales, relationship, sector and local duties must be checked for actual parties, places and activities.

title: Nebraska: a filed franchise notice does not settle the relationship law
description: The independent Franchise Practices Act has its own definition, scope and termination conditions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Research the second state-law test
paragraphs: A Nebraska SAMP notice and the Franchise Practices Act answer different questions. The latter has its own franchise definition and cumulative scope criteria. Its sales figures are criteria for that law, not a general definition of an SME or minimum size for U.S. expansion.

sections.heading: A service company must investigate the place of business
paragraphs: The Act defines a fixed place where the franchisee displays and sells goods or offers and sells the franchisor’s services, and expressly excludes an office, warehouse, storage place, residence or vehicle. Whether a proposed operating location meets the actual test requires facts; do not assume that having a state address is sufficient.

sections.heading: Record all three application criteria
paragraphs: Section 87-403 requires the stated Nebraska place of business, gross sales of covered products or services between franchisor and franchisee exceeding $35,000 in the 12 months immediately preceding the institution of suit, and more than 20 percent of the franchisee’s gross sales intended to be or derived from the franchise. Those criteria are cumulative. They are not an annual revenue floor for every business entering Nebraska.

Section 87-402 has distinct nonalcoholic-beverage wording and excludes petroleum arrangements from its franchise definition. The source also defines franchise fee and good cause. Retain the actual payment and business facts rather than importing the federal definition.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a B2B field-service operator
paragraphs: A Dutch service operator works from an office and travels to customer sites. The team records what is sold at or from each location, the branded rights, the relevant payment structure and sales between the parties. It leaves application of the relationship statute pending review rather than copying a conclusion from a retail-shop example.

sections.heading: Do not make the notice period universal
paragraphs: 87-404 generally combines written notice of reasons at least 60 days in advance with good cause, but includes an abandonment branch and specified grounds with immediate-notice treatment. It also contains noncompetition provisions with separate scope. No proposed termination should be released solely because a generic calendar says 60 days have passed.

Section 87-404(1) also preserves a contract provision that the franchise is not renewable or is renewable only if stated reasonable conditions are met. A renewal date therefore needs the actual contractual and statutory branch; the good-cause language alone is not a promise of indefinite renewal.

sections.heading: Evidence for the relationship reviewer
bullets: Actual locations and how customers obtain goods or services.
Trademark rights, payments and community-of-interest facts.
The relevant 12 month sales between parties and franchisee sales allocation.
Contract term, renewal terms, claimed defaults and contemporaneous supporting records.
Document the applicable statutory branch, agreement conditions and actual notice before termination or enforcement.

practicalOutput: A separate Franchise Practices Act applicability and relationship-action checklist.
limitations: This page researches the named issue; it is not a complete state franchise or operating-law survey.
Federal disclosure and any independent state sales, relationship, sector and local duties must be checked for actual parties, places and activities.
